column3: By the end of grade 6, students will advance in oral communication, not only capturing explicit information but also inferring deeper meanings and interpreting speaker intentions with more sophistication. They will express complex ideas more fluently, employing a broader vocabulary and coordinated connectors, and refine their use of nonverbal communication. Their reading skills will include a thorough analysis of texts, distinguishing subtle differences and making inferences to construct meaning, and their writing will reflect an improved ability to adapt texts to the audience, develop ideas around central themes, and employ cohesive devices for well-organized paragraphs.
column4: By the end of grade 7, students will be skilled in orally communicating in English, able to infer and interpret detailed information from conversations and texts, including the intentions behind spoken words. They will effectively use nonverbal and paraverbal cues to enhance their speech, organize ideas around central themes using relevant vocabulary and grammar, and actively participate in discussions about familiar and past events. Their reading will involve critically engaging with texts to integrate information, make inferences, and evaluate language use. In writing, they will produce medium-length texts that are clearly organized, using cohesive devices and a mix of everyday and complex grammar for clarity, reflecting on their work with insight.
column5: By the end of grade 8, students will refine their oral communication to more deeply understand and convey complex information, using nuanced nonverbal cues for emphasis and engaging in sophisticated exchanges on a broad range of topics. They will critically read texts, integrating advanced elements and making inferences to construct comprehensive interpretations, and apply critical thinking to evaluate texts' language and intentions. In writing, they will adeptly tailor texts to specific audiences and purposes, organizing ideas into coherent, structured paragraphs with sophisticated vocabulary and grammar, ensuring clarity through precise orthography, and engaging in thoughtful reflection and evaluation of their written work.
column6: By the end of grade 9, students will have developed the ability to communicate orally in English across a range of texts, interpreting the speaker’s intentions and adapting their speech to both formal and informal situations with clear pronunciation and intonation. They will organize and express their ideas around themes using cohesive resources and a specialized vocabulary. In discussions, they will begin to reflect on and evaluate their own and others' ideas, participating actively on a variety of topics. Their reading skills will include critically engaging with complex texts, starting to integrate and interpret conflicting information, and reflecting on the text's form and content. Writing skills will involve creating extended texts for specific audiences, organizing ideas into paragraphs, using relevant vocabulary and medium complexity grammar, and reflecting on their language use to enhance clarity.
column7: By the end of grade 10, students will enhance their oral communication skills, using nonverbal and paraverbal cues more effectively to underscore their messages, and evaluating spoken content with greater insight. They will express themselves with increased fluency, employing a more idiomatic language range and engaging in complex interactions. In reading, they will adeptly integrate main ideas with specific details to construct the overall meaning of texts, evaluating language use and the text’s impact with an understanding of their socio-cultural context. In writing, they will produce more sophisticated texts, structuring their ideas with greater clarity using subheadings and varied grammatical constructions, and critically evaluating their work for improvement.
column8: By the end of grade 11, students will master oral communication in English, speaking with clarity and fluency across a broad spectrum of topics, skillfully interpreting interlocutors' intentions and counter-arguing when necessary. They will adeptly adapt their speech to various contexts, using an extensive and accurate range of language. Their critical reading skills will be highly developed, allowing them to interpret texts by integrating complex information and evaluating texts' language and effects based on deep socio-cultural understanding. Writing skills will include crafting extended, reflective texts with advanced organization and development of ideas, employing a wide range of cohesive devices and specialized vocabulary, and using orthographic resources for utmost clarity. Students will reflect on and evaluate their texts with a sophisticated understanding of language use, aiming for continuous improvement.
